full_judgment:
Mr. Bijan Kumar Das J:  By this rule the opposite parties Nos. 1-3 were called upon to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 12.8.2004 passed by the learned District judge, Patuakhali in Title Appeal No. 92 of 2004 summarily rejecting to admit the appeal upon affirming the judgment and decree dated 22.3.2004 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge-in-charge, Patukhali in Title Suit No. 13 of 1999 decreeing the suit exparte should not be set asaid and or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 1(Ka)-1(chha) and 2 were contesting the suit by filing a written statement. Ultimately the suit was fixed for peremptory hearing on 22.3.2004 which was also fixed for payment of CP cost of Tk. 5,000/- by the defendants. The trial court took up hearing of the suit but the contesting defendants did not turn up and the trial court examined P.W.1 and exhibited the documents and then decreed the suit exparte in preliminary form on 22.3.2004 with a cost of Tk. 10,000/- Against the said exparte decree the contesting defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 92 of 2004 before the learned District judge, Patuakhali. The learned District Judge by the impugned judgment dated 12.8.2004 held that the appeal cannot be admitted as it was not maintainable due to the Third Amendment of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 5. Mr. Abdul Awal, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the learned Advocate Mr. Md. Mozibur Rahman has placed the impugned judgment before me and submits that the learned District Judge committed a gross error of law in rejecting the appeal summarily on the finding that the appellant had his remedy under order 17 rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure holding' The lower court rightly decreed the suit exparte for non-payment adjournment cost as per the CPC (Third Amendment) Act, 2003. As per the said amendment the appellant/defendant may take shelter under order 17 rule (7) CPC. Thus- this civil appeal cannot be admitted and liable to be rejected." Mr. Awal submits that the defendant has statutory right to prefer an appeal under section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure or could have complained for setting aside the exparte decree under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure or could have prayed for review of the judgment and decree under order 47 rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure or could file a suit challenging the exparte decree on the ground of fraud. The learned Advocate submits that the amendment of the Code of Civil Procedure by inserting the provision in order 17 rule 7(7) does not take way the other vested rights available to the defendants but this is a special provision for speedy disposal of the exparte judgments and decrees. In order 17, rule 3,4,5,6 and 7 have been inserted which all are aimed at speedy disposal of the litigation and also restricting the courts with respect to adjournments. Under rule 3 of order 17 the courts are not now permitted to grant more that six adjournments in a suit before peremptory hearing at the instance of either party. to the suit, and any adjournment granted to a party beyond the aforesaid limit shall make such party liable to pay a cost of not less than two hundred take and not more than one thousand taka to the other party, within time to be specified by it; noncompliance with which, by the plaintiff shall render the suit liable to the dismissed and, by the defendant shall render the suit liable to be disposed of exparte and provided that the court shall not grant more than three adjournments to a party even with cost under this rule. In the impugned judgment the learned District Judge' has clearly mentioned that the defendant appellant, who take shelter under order 17 rule 7 which provides that a suit dismissed 'or disposed of exparte under sub-rule (3) at (4) shall not be revived for hearing unless the party, for whose noncompliance the suit was dismissed or disposed of exparte, makes within thirty days of such dismissal or exparte disposal, an application together with cost of two thousand take into Court for such revival; and upon such application being made, the suit shall be revived for hearing without any further proceeding; and cost deposited into Court shall be paid to the other party. This amended provision of order 17 rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure was included for speedy disposal of the litigation and this amendment does not, in any way, debar a party from availing his other legal remedies including filing an appeal under section 96(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure which is always available to a defendant against whom an exparte decree has been passed. The learned District Judge was therefore not correct in its decision that the appeal cannot be admitted as not maintainable as per CPC (Third Amendment) 2003. 

 8. The stay of operation of the impugned judgment and decree as passed at the time of issuance of the rule and extended subsequently is hereby vacated.
